root_cause.text: The cc1352_bootloader_rx() function in the gb-beagleplay driver copies incoming serdev chunks into a fixed-size rx_buffer without checking whether the chunk fits within the remaining buffer space, leading to a buffer overflow when multiple packets or leftover bytes accumulate.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds a bounds check (`if (count > sizeof(bg->rx_buffer) - bg->rx_buffer_len)`) and drops oversized data, and the commit description explains that because leftover bytes may persist between callbacks and multiple packets may arrive in one chunk, the count is not constrained by a single packet length, so unchecked memcpy can overflow the buffer.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add a guard to prevent buffer overflow when receiving oversized bootloader data chunks.
intent_record.what: Added a conditional check that compares the incoming data count against the remaining space in the receive buffer; if it exceeds, it logs a warning, resets the buffer length to zero, and returns early.
intent_record.how: Prevents buffer overflow by discarding oversized data chunks and resetting the buffer state, avoiding out-of-bounds memory write.
